summary: FY2025/26 (May 2025–Apr 2026): 21,483.41 t FFB, 28.22 t/ha vs 29.32 budget and 32.10 a year earlier (-12%); PA calls it 2.4% below budget, it is 3.75% (PA, Agro).
Ex-estate cost RM263.90/t vs RM258.17 budget (+2%); harvesting & collection RM121.11/t is the overrun (infield loading RM7.94 vs 2.69) (PA).
Yields fell in 9 of 10 plantings; Agro blames dry spells Jan–Mar and May–Aug 2025 (FY25/26 rainfall 1,866 mm) and ageing palms; P2010 still best at 32.63 t/ha.
Ganoderma about 9% (8,348 palms, Oct 2025), worst P2001 18%; new census and palm census in progress (PA, Agro).
Weeding behind: circle 1.3 of 3 rounds, selective 2 of 3 (PA); manuring done but up to 5 months late (Agro); labour adequate at 74 workers vs 76 required (PA).

issues.title: FFB shortfall stated as 2–2.4%, actually 3.75%
issues.detail: PA 8.1 and 11.12 say 21,483.41 t was 2.40% below the 22,320 t budget, and item 16 says 2% below a budget of 22,300.00 t. 21,483.41 vs 22,320 is -3.75% (836.59 t); yield 28.22 vs 29.32 t/ha is also -3.75%. Item 16 budget 22,300 t differs from Tables 22/23 (22,320 t). Section 8.1 also labels 22,320 t as 'tons per hectare'.

issues.title: Cost of production RM263.90 or RM261.90/t
issues.detail: PA Table 24, item 17 and 9.1 give ex-estate COP RM263.90/t (2% above RM258.17). Concluding remark 11.13 says RM261.90/t.

issues.title: Harvest cost ex-external transport: RM82.90 vs RM89.20/t
issues.detail: PA Table 22 sub-total before external transport is RM82.90/t (budget 78.30), +5.9%. Section 7.14 says this cost was RM89.20/t, 14% above RM78.30. Table 22 actual items add to 82.95 and RM1,781,845 (printed 1,781,847); budget items add to 78.25/t (1,746,604 / 22,320). Table 22 total RM121.12/t vs Table 24 RM121.11/t (2,601,816 / 21,483.41 = 121.11).

issues.title: Harvesting intervals: 'below 15 days throughout' vs 18–24 days
issues.detail: PA item 15, 7.11 and 11.11 say intervals were kept at or below 15 days throughout FY2025/26. Agro Table 10 shows Jun 2025 up to 18–20 days, Jul 2025 20–24 days in most plantings and Aug 2025 up to 17–19 days; Agro 5.3 says intervals were extended Jun–Sep 2025. PA Table 21 itself shows 15–16 days in 2000A and 2003A1 in Apr 2026.

issues.title: Boundary cost RM785 vs RM1,307.60
issues.detail: PA 6.9.3 says boundary/survey/fences cost RM785 (RM1.03/ha), 'in line with budget'. PA Table 6 shows RM1,307.60 (RM1.72/ha) with no budget.

issues.title: Harvester output 1.60–1.90 vs 3.00 t/man-day
issues.detail: PA 7.3, Table 19 and item 15 give harvester output 1.60–1.90 t/man-day (low); PA 7.7 and Table 20 say harvester productivity in April was 3.00 t/man-day, 'acceptable'.

issues.title: Ganoderma 2003A1 and census totals differ PA vs Agro
issues.detail: Same census (Oct 2025) printed twice. 2003A1: PA Table 15 1,891 healthy palms, 441 Ganoderma, 19%; Agro Table 8 2,590 palms, 320 infected, 12%. Both print totals 96,083 / 8,348 but the PA columns add to 95,384 / 8,469 (Agro columns do add up). PA total shows 9%, Agro 8% (8,348/96,083 = 8.7%). Both cover only 717.47 ha: 2003B1 and B2 (43.69 ha) are missing. PA Table 15 total SPH printed as 122, but 96,083 palms / 717.47 ha = 134.

issues.title: Selective spraying 1,562.45 ha (PA) vs 1,542.45 ha (Agro)
issues.detail: PA Table 9: 1,562.45 ha, with 2003A 152 ha and 2014 9.02 ha. Agro Table 6: 1,542.45 ha, 2003A1+A2 128.44 ha and 2014A+B 12.58 ha. PA 2014 9.02 of 27.06 ha shown as 46% (=33%). Agro 4.4.2 says overall weeding was 55% of programme.

issues.title: Circle spraying total 1,001.46 ha (PA) but fields add to 1,002.62
issues.detail: PA Table 7 and 6.1.4.1 print 1,001.46 ha done (44%), but the field rows add to 1,002.62 ha, which is the Agro Table 6 total. Agro Table 6 programme is 2,329.12 ha vs PA 2,283.48 ha: Agro 2011B circle programme is 114.10 ha where 3 rounds of 22.82 ha = 68.46 ha (inflates the total by 45.64 ha), so Agro shows 43% instead of 44%.

issues.title: Manuring 959.27 mt 100% (PA) vs 958.43 of 959.22 mt (Agro)
issues.detail: PA Table 11 shows 959.27 mt applied = programme, 100% for every field. Agro Table 3: programme 959.22 mt, delivered 959.24, applied 958.43 mt; 0.79 mt NK Mix not applied (nursery area). Agro Table 4 lists delays of 2–5 months (P14A Mix B scheduled May, done Oct 2025), but Agro 5.11(b) says delays were 'up to three months'. PA 6.2.8 calls the RM1,317.73/ha manuring cost a '6-month period'; the table is 12 months.

issues.title: Labour table variance column wrong
issues.detail: PA Table 4 variance column: cutters and carriers 24 vs 23 required shown as -2 each (should be +1); harvesting mandore 1 vs 2 shown 0 (should be -1); loose fruit collector 1 vs 2 shown 1 (-1); field mandore 2 vs 1 shown 0 (+1); manuring 4 vs 5 shown 1 (-1); gate security 2 vs 3 shown 1 (-1). Rows where actual = requirement (0) and the tractor driver row (-1) are right; grand total 74 vs 76 (-2) is right.

issues.title: Barn owl occupancy totals
issues.detail: PA Table 13: Feb 2026 field figures add to 24 occupied boxes, printed total 23 (30%); Aug 2025 fields add to 16, printed 17.

issues.title: Soil mounding cost RM27,000 vs about RM32,000
issues.detail: PA Table 16 and 6.4.1: 3,750 palms x RM7.20 = RM27,000. Section 6.4.4 says unbudgeted soil mounding was about RM32,000 (plus about RM16,000 for irrigation pump and pump house).

issues.title: Vehicle table: WSR 3296 hours and WTY 4487 rate
issues.detail: PA Table 25: Landini WSR 3296 total 1,174 hours but average monthly running shown as 13,098 hours (budget 102). Landini WTY 4487: RM47,357.83 / 596 hrs = RM79.46/hr, printed RM76.46/hr (text 10.1b uses 76.46 and +402%; at 79.46 it is +422% over RM15.22).

issues.title: Labels and units
issues.detail: PA 7.10 says 2003A1 and 2001A achieved '23 and 26 days' (Table 21: rounds). PA 7.13(d) external transport budget 'RM35.00 per hectare' (per tonne). PA 6.6.2 backhoe 'RM52.50 per hectare' (Table 17: per hour). Bagworm Table 14 gives 2012A as 59.72 ha (block is 54.26 ha). Page headers read 'Visit for 2-2025' while the cover says visit for 1/2026. Agro 5.5 gives P00 yield 24.0 t/ha (Table 9: 24.23). PA 6.1.4.7 gives RM16.00/ha for the flat area and RM14.50 for terraces, but Table 8 and 6.1.4.6 pay RM16.00 in the hilly/terraced fields (03B, 05B, 11...). PA 7.3 says harvest rates RM37–39/t, Table 19 has RM36.00 (2005A, 2003B RM45).

issues.title: General charges budget per ha
issues.detail: PA Table 5 budget RM426.00/718.00/524.00 per ha and total RM1,668.00; Appendix 1 shows RM426.78/717.57/523.72 and RM1,668.07 for the same budget.

actions.item: Bring circle spraying up to date (1.3 of 3 rounds; overdue P01A, P03B2, P03B3, P12C)
Complete inter-row/selective rounds; eradicate Clidemia, Tetracera, Stenochlaena, VOPs and woodies (triclopyr + diesel)
Restack pruned fronds away from palm circles (halved, between palms or along terrace lips)
Avoid further FY2026/27 manuring delays caused by late fertiliser deliveries
Fix fertiliser placement in P12C (narrow bands, near mounding holes)
Find cause of wet floor in fertiliser store and keep it dry
Finish palm census (due end Jul 2026), verify P11A/B SPH; complete annual Ganoderma census
Water availability assessment for the nursery pond; source Ganoderma-free soil medium
Mound remaining ~3,000 palms; continue deboling of Ganoderma points
Raise harvester output from 1.6–1.9 to 2.5–3.0 t/man-day; monitor machine and harvester productivity monthly
Keep harvesting intervals at 15 days or less, especially in peak months
Clean barn owl boxes yearly (PA); census occupancy again in six months (Agro)
Use census/thinning allocation: thin runt palms in 2010, 2011, 2012, 2014
Consider semi-mechanised manuring (electric Badang/mini crawler) and CDA for circle spraying
Write off old, damaged Landini tractors with high running cost
Patch steep hilly roads with crusher run; keep security patrols so FFB is not left at boundary overnight
Keep a systematic record of beneficial predator host plants
Extend woody and epiphyte poisoning to remaining overgrown boundary areas and the whole estate

kb:
LEONG HIN SAN ESTATE, Leong Hin San Sdn Bhd (United Malacca Berhad, UMB group). Fact pack from PA Report 1/2026 (Planting Advisor En. Adnan Bin Mustafa, visit 18 June 2026, previous visit 17 December 2025, review period May 2025 to April 2026, 12 months = financial year 2025/2026) and Agronomy Report 1/2026 (Agronomist Mr Chong Kuan Ming, visit 23 June 2026, previous visit 13 November 2025, manuring programme FY2026/2027). Estate Manager Mr Livindran A/L Ganesan. Plantation Controller (Peninsular Malaysia) Mr Low Fook Sin, who joined both visits. The financial year runs May to April, so all "year" figures below are FY periods (FY2025/26 = May 2025 to April 2026). Single estate, single division (Division: Main); no combined figures.

AREA (PA Table 1 and 2, Agro Table 1, as of April 2026): title 844.68 ha; planted 761.16 ha (90.11% of title), all mature, no immature, no replanting; roads 73.90 ha, buildings/others 9.62 ha. Plantings: 2000 74.00 ha (A 33.54, B 40.46), 2001 50.12 (A), 2002 93.08 (A 54.28, B 38.80), 2003A 64.22 (1 20.89, 2 43.33), 2003B 89.56 (1 11.04, 2 32.65, 3 45.87), 2005 57.88 (A 29.12, B 28.76), 2010 117.17 (A 32.13, B 44.62, C 15.49, D 24.93), 2011 64.92 (A 42.10, B 22.82), 2012 141.19 (A 54.26, B 47.06, C 39.87), 2014 9.02 (A 5.46, B 3.56). All DxP (IOI; 2005 Guthrie, 2010 Sime Darby, 2014 mixed). PA: no replanting for the next two years since the 26-year-old 2000 planting is manageable; 2000A and 2000B yields to April 2026 were 25.65 and 23.06 t/ha. Agro: about 10% of palms over 25 years; replanting P00 not recommended yet (yield satisfactory, palms short); 20 to 25-year-olds are the largest share; prime plantings 44% of area. Nursery: a 3.0 ha oil palm nursery for 30,000 seedlings per season is being prepared in P03A2, using the existing pond and pump. Agro: assess pond water supply against peak irrigation demand; bring in Ganoderma-free soil medium.

PALM CENSUS (Agro Table 2, latest 2/2024 SPH): range 112 (2003A1) to 158 (2011A); 2000A 116, 2000B 127, 2010A 130, 2011B 152. Agro says the data look outdated and P11A/P11B over 148 SPH (+10% on the previous census) is unusually high; a new palm census is due to finish by end July 2026.

STAFF (PA Table 3, April 2026): Assistant Manager Kumaravel A/L Natarajan (joined 1 Oct 2025), a field supervisor, a general clerk, a chief clerk and two trainees (Nov 2025, May 2026). Field supervisor on SOCSO leave since 18 October (accident); extra trainee recruited. Satisfactory.

LABOUR (PA Table 4, April 2026): 74 workers (68 checkroll, 6 contract) vs 76 required, 1 per 10 ha. Harvesters 48 (24 cutters, 24 carriers) vs 46 required, 1 per 16 ha, adequate with mechanised infield collection. Sprayers 7 (1:109 ha), manuring 4 vs 5 (1:190 ha), security 2 vs 3. The 6 contract harvesters hired by Nov 2025 had left; Machap Estate harvesters can help in peak months.

GENERAL CHARGES (PA Table 5 and Appendix 1, FY2025/26): RM1,295,518.66 vs budget RM1,269,668 (2% over), RM1,702.03/ha vs RM1,668.00. Management and supervision RM283,495.42 (RM372.45/ha vs 426.00); labour and amenities RM587,631.66 (RM772.02 vs 718.00); other expenditure RM424,391.58 (RM557.56 vs 524.00). Overruns above 10%: labour wages +RM4,954 (10%); labour EPF +RM18,032 (46%, 2% EPF for foreign workers from Oct 2025); labour welfare +RM10,952 (74%, support for Batu Anan and Machap harvesters); general office +RM7,965 (25%, incl. best estate award RM5,000); water/electricity +RM42,069 (78%, bills and an underground leak; RM95,948.82 vs 53,880); transport and travelling +RM16,100 (60%, vehicle MCN5213, towing, crane transport from Sabah RM11,554.16); other building maintenance +RM18,817 (276%, guard house, repairs, painting for the Director's visit, MSPO preparation). Acceptable.

UPKEEP AND CULTIVATION (PA Table 6, FY2025/26): RM1,772,149.36 vs RM1,965,157 budget; RM2,328.23/ha vs RM2,581.79. Per ha actual vs budget: upkeep supervision 69.28 vs 59.24; weeding 174.46 vs 272.48 (-36%); manuring 1,317.73 vs 1,638.42 (-20%; RM1,003,000.15); pest and disease 54.26 vs 80.87 (RM41,296.83); census and thinning nil vs 10.10; drains 8.41 vs 28.01; roads and bridges 461.93 vs 316.53 (+46%, RM351,599.80); soil and water conservation 75.49 vs 3.87 (RM57,461.37, unbudgeted mounding about RM32,000 and about RM16,000 pump servicing and pump-house extension); boundaries 1.72, unbudgeted (RM1,307.60; text 6.9.3 says RM785, RM1.03/ha, 'in line with budget'); pruning 164.95 vs 165.72; tools nil vs 6.57.

WEEDING (PA): Circle and path spraying 1,001.46 of 2,283.48 ha (field rows actually add to 1,002.62 ha), 1.3 of 3.0 rounds (44%): 2000 1.5 rounds, 2002 and 2003A 2.0, 2005 1.8, others 1.0. Selective spraying 1,562.45 ha, 2.0 rounds (68%); 2010 2.5 rounds; 2011 40%; 2014 1 round. Delay because sprayers were sent to help harvesting in the high-crop first half; some fields deliberately deferred since circles were clean. Woody poisoning 423.93 ha, epiphyte poisoning 129.14 ha, circle raking 74 ha in 2000 (all done). Sprayers 4.5 to 5.0 ha/man-day, RM71 to 72.50/day. Target Tetracera, Stenochlaena, VOPs and woody shrubs at terrace edges; consider CDA for circles. Agro Table 6: inter-row 1,542.45 of 2,283.48 ha (68%), circle 1,002.62 of 2,329.12 ha (43%); most fields only 2 interrow and 1 circle round; overall 55% of programme, due to labour diverted to harvesting and deferment. Second circle round not completed in most fields, especially prime plantings. Circle weeding overdue in P01A, P03B2, P03B3, P12C; Ageratum in P03B1, P10C, P11A circles; Clidemia hirta patches; VOPs in P11A and P03B. Tetracera and Imperata reduced. Remove large woodies by slashing or triclopyr plus diesel.

MANURING: PA Table 11: FY2025/26 programme 959.27 mt fully applied (100%): RP 81.32, NK mix 245.40, Mix A 203.30, Mix B 399.87, kieserite 29.38 mt. Manual broadcasting (wheelbarrow on flat, bucket on terraces), quality satisfactory. 4.5 to 6 ha/man-day, RM66 to 72/day. Semi-mechanised application (electric Badang or mini crawler) recommended for 35 to 40 bags/day. Agro Table 3: programme 959.22 mt, delivered 959.24, applied 958.43 mt (NK Mix 244.60 of 245.39; 0.79 mt ceased at nursery area). Agro Table 4: delays of 2 to 5 months on NK mixture (P01A, P02A, P02B, P03A1), Mix A (P03A, P05), Mix B (P10A, P10D, P11, P12, P14; P14A May to Oct 2025) and RP (P05, P10D, P11, Dec 2025 to Feb 2026). FY2026/27 manuring started but hit by late deliveries. June 2026 Mix A, Mix B and kieserite stock on pallets but wet floor in store (find cause: hygroscopic fertiliser, roof leak or tractors). P12C quality: narrow bands and fertiliser close to mounding holes in frond rows; broadcast evenly in weeded circles. Leaf analysis July 2025 showed suboptimal Mg, mainly older plantings.

FY2026/27 FERTILISER PROGRAMME (Agro Appendix 1, grams per palm; no revision needed): 2000 and 2001 Mix A 2500 x3 (Jun, Oct, Feb); 2002 Mix A 2000 x4; 2003A and 2003B Mix A 2000 x4 plus kieserite 1000 (Jul); 2005 Mix A 2000 x4 (Jul, Oct, Jan, Apr); 2010A/B Mix B 2500 (Jul), 2200 (Oct), RP 1500 (Dec), Mix B 2500 (Jan), Mix A 2200 (Apr); 2010C/D Mix B 2500 (May), 2200 (Aug), 2500 (Nov), RP 1500 (Dec), Mix B 2200 (Feb); 2011 and 2012 Mix B 2200 x4, kieserite 1000 (Jun), RP 1500 (Dec); 2014 kieserite 1000, Mix B 2200 to 2500 x4 (A x3), RP 1700. Mix A = 45% SOA, 40% MOP, 15% kieserite; Mix B = 45% SOA, 40% MOP, 14% kieserite, 1% borate. FY2027/28 programme to be drawn up in the second half of the year.

PESTS AND DISEASES: Rats: insignificant (Agro Table 7 monthly damage 1 to 6%), no baiting; some damage near platforms in prime plantings. Barn owls (PA Table 13): 76 boxes, 1 per 10 ha; occupancy Feb 2026 23 boxes (30%), still low; no cleaning done, clean yearly. Agro: damaged boxes replaced, census again in six months. Bagworm: Promax (deltamethrin) 10 ml per 10 L on 38 ha in 2012A and 2012C, 2 rounds (PA); no recurrence (Agro). Predator host plants seen but not systematically recorded (PA). Ganoderma (census Oct 2025, PA Table 15 and Agro Table 8): 8,348 infected of 96,083 palms on 717.47 ha, about 9% (PA) / 8% (Agro). Worst: 2001A 18% (1,163 palms), 2000B 13%, 2000A 12%, 2003A1 19% (PA) or 12% (Agro), 2005A 10%; lowest 2010D and 2014B 3%. 2003B1 and B2 not in the census. PA: standing-palm basis understates the true rate (dead and fallen palms not counted). Agro: over 5% in most fields; new census started; mitigation by palm mounding in P10, P11, P12 and deboling; sanitation at replanting for older fields. Mounding: 3,750 palms in 2010A at RM7.20 = RM27,000; about 3,000 more to do (PA). Cattle intrusion unresolved, damage to lower fronds in P12A/B (Agro). Census and thinning: nil spent of RM7,684 budget; use it for censuses and thinning runts in 2010 to 2014. Agro: thinning in P11 improved light.

ROADS, DRAINS, BOUNDARY (PA): road grading and laterite 2,700 chains at RM212/chain as budgeted; culvert backhoe RM3,780; pothole repair RM6,016.92; roadside frond pruning RM5,227.30. Roads passable; patch steep hilly sections with crusher run. Drains satisfactory (RM6,405, RM8.41/ha). Boundary drain clear; guards must patrol and FFB must not be left at the boundary overnight.

PRUNING: PA Table 18: 3 of 3 progressive rounds on all 761.16 ha, RM164.95/ha, good appearance; stack fronds slanting between palms, changed gradually. Agro Table 5: all done except P11A final round; minimal over-pruning; fronds still too close to circles in terraced areas: halve and stack between palms or on terrace lips.

PALM APPEARANCE (Agro): orange-frond Mg deficiency in hilly/ravine P03 (B2, B3) and a few palms in P10-P12, reduced since last visit.

HARVESTING (PA): 48 checkroll harvesters; 10 electric mini crawlers leased from Agrostar (PA 7.2 says RM500 per month), 4 harvesters per machine, 9.87 t/machine/day; box crane 65 t/day (532.81 ha) and Solaris crane 35 t/day (228.35 ha). Harvester output 1.60 to 1.90 t/man-day (most 1.80; but 7.7 and Table 20 say 3.00 in April with mini crawlers) at RM36 to 45/t, earning RM64.80 to RM72.00/day; 2003B very steep, 1.60 t at RM45/t. Target 2.5 to 3.0 t/day for RM90 to 120/day. Table 21 April 2026: 2 rounds a month, 24 rounds a year, 15-day intervals (2000A and 2003A1 15-16 days; 2001A 26 rounds, 2003A1 23). Agro: intervals acceptable, only two sub-blocks in P10A slightly over 15 days; crop recovery improved in P03B2; bunch ripeness and loose fruit fine in P10C; debris in circles P03B1, P10C. Agro Table 10 monthly intervals: Jul 2025 20-24 days in most plantings (P11, P12 16-18, P14 13-16), Jun up to 18-20 (P2000), Aug up to 17-19 (P2002); from Oct 2025 mostly 9 to 18 days (2003A 17-18 and 2003B 18-19 in Jan 2026), April 2026 8 to 16 days.

HARVESTING AND COLLECTION COST (PA Table 22, FY2025/26, RM/t actual vs budget): harvesting own FFB 44.45 vs 46.67; internal transport 21.60 vs 21.34; infield loading 7.94 vs 2.69 (+195%, manual loading when the box crane grabber broke); unbudgeted contractor 2.44 (terminated) and loose fruit collection 0.99; sub-total 82.90 vs 78.30; external transport 38.17 vs 35.00; total RM2,601,816, RM121.12/t vs 113.25 (3% over). Text 7.14 quotes cost to ramp as RM89.20/t.

CROP (PA Table 23 and Agro Table 9, FY2025/26 May 2025 to Apr 2026): FFB 21,483.41 t vs budget 22,320 t and 24,430.42 t in FY2024/25. Yield 28.22 t/ha vs 29.32 budget and 32.10 last year (-12.1%). CPO 4,183.09 t (OER 19.47% vs 20.00% budget, 19.92% last year), kernel 1,077.49 t (KER 5.02% vs 5.00%), CPO 5.50 t/ha vs 5.86 budget and 6.39 last year.
